scope: REQUIREMENTS.md Part A §5-9: handoff/compaction/adoption signal, journal and session lifecycle, notify, display renderer (S1/S2), agent-dir resolution (U2) (packages/nana-pack) — 33 off-form origins split or merged per design-ruling.md §2
notes: Two merges found (R-142, R-193): in both, the implementation produces the two clauses' observable effects through ONE unconditional code path with no branch that could satisfy one half while breaking the other, so a split would hand the second clause either the origin's exact cite set (the sibling-cite shape the lane exists to catch) or an untested status on evidence the first clause already claims. R-142: nana-handoff.ts's pickup block builds ONE literal `Source: ... update ${loc.text} in place.` string from a single `loc` value — mutating to drop the custom path (keep "in place") or to drop "in place" (keep the path) each turns the SAME two custom-path assertions red together, and a source-level override of `loc.text` breaks the default-store scenario's independent assertion too, confirming one shared, unconditional rendering step. R-193: lib/config.ts's loadConfig, when the active user file is absent, never reads the stranded default file at all (`// Never read it.`) and sets gate to built-in defaults in the same branch — there is no code path that reads-but-ignores versus simply not-reading. One overclaim caught and corrected before judgement, not after a review round: R-166's two pre-existing cites (`f: a working notifier raises/writes no fallback`) hold identically whether the OS notifier call is ever invoked at all — verified by commenting out every `darwinNotify`/`windowsNotify`/OSC-777 call site: both cited assertions stayed green. So R-166's own clause ("a working OS notifier shall be used") drops to untested; the surviving clause ("no fallback … raised or journaled") keeps both cites under a new id. New-row status defaults to 'untested' unless an existing cited test, read directly and independently, pins that clause by an assertion that would fail if the clause broke; when in doubt, untested, per design-ruling.md §2. Every implemented split below was proved by an actual mutation run in a disposable copy of the source (git-reverted after each check) — not merely read and reasoned about; the full list is in the worker report. 34 clause slots were needed for 33 origins (31 split 1-for-1, 2 split 1-for-2: R-120, R-181) minus 2 merges (R-142, R-193) = 33 new rows, R-795 to R-827, inside the pack's declared continuation block R-756-879 (A1 used R-756-794; 52 numbers remain free after this batch).

merged.reason: "the prompt shall name that file, never .pi/handoff.md" and "shall say to update it in place" are rendered by ONE literal template string (nana-handoff.ts: `Source: ... update ${loc.text} in place.`) built from a single `loc` value with no conditional between the two halves; the custom-path test's own assertion requires BOTH the correct path AND the exact "in place" wording in one `includes()` call, so every mutation tried (wrong path kept "in place"; correct path dropped "in place"; a source-level override of `loc.text`) turned the SAME assertion red for both reasons at once, the sibling-cite shape the lane exists to avoid. Rewritten to one shall sentence; same three pre-existing cites, no marker change.

lib/config.ts's loadConfig: `if (!user.present) { gate = {...gateLeaves(undefined), stopReason: null}; ... never read it }` is ONE unconditional branch — the stranded default file is never opened AND its content never influences `gate` in the same statement group. There is no implementation path that reads the file but discards its denies versus one that never reads it; splitting would make the second clause either untested on the first's exact evidence or cite the identical assertions. Rewritten to one shall sentence; same three pre-existing cites, no marker change.
